basic_info.name: Kantesti (Kantesti AI Blood Test Analyzer; kantesti.net, free-access program at kantesti.org)
basic_info.category: AI lab-test interpreter (B2C upload-and-interpret tool with aspirational B2B/enterprise API layer)
basic_info.country: Registered UK (Kantesti Ltd, London, Companies House #17090423, incorporated 2026-03-13); sole director Emirhan Bulut, Turkish national born Nov 2001 residing in Turkey; markets 'Made in Germany' on homepage; sells globally in 75+ languages with heavy PT-BR localized SEO targeting Brazil
basic_info.stage: Startup (~5 months old at research date 2026-08-22), in aggressive programmatic-SEO growth mode; products shipped (web, iOS, Android, Chrome extension, API v11) but scale claims far outpace verifiable traction
basic_info.pricing_model: Freemium + per-report + annual package: Free tier = 1 basic report (no PDF export, no trends, no family profiles, no nutrition plans); single report EUR 9.99; 6-report bundle ('most popular', 2 family profiles); annual EUR 49.99/year = 12 reports (homepage says family sharing up to 3 profiles, pricing page says 5 — inconsistent); aggressive 60%-off discount codes (VIP60) pushed site-wide; regional pricing EUR (EU) / GBP (UK) / USD (everywhere else — Brazil pays USD, no BRL, no PIX; payments via Stripe, Azure Marketplace, bank transfer, and cryptocurrency BTC/ETH/USDT); 30-day refund on annual; Enterprise/API custom pricing. Application-based 100% free program at kantesti.org for people in financial hardship (human-reviewed applications). No price changes observed in-window, but constant discount-code marketing creates fake-urgency pricing.
basic_info.target_user: Primary: lay patients wanting to understand blood test results without waiting for a doctor; secondary: prosumers/biohackers (trends, nutrition); tertiary (aspirational pitch): labs, hospital CIOs, insurers, telemedicine platforms via B2B buyer's guide
basic_info.scale_metrics: Semi-verifiable: 100,000+ Android downloads (Google Play, '197 countries'), iOS app rated 4.8 but from only 5 ratings, Trustpilot 4.0 from 21 reviews. Unverifiable marketing claims: 2M+ users, 127+ countries, 50,000+ doctors worldwide, 2.5M blood tests analyzed, 98% satisfaction, advisory board of 50+ physicians (validation page names only 4). A company incorporated 2026-03-13 cannot plausibly have 2M users/50k doctors — treat scale claims as noise. Durable threat is not the user base: it is the SEO machine (~960 PT articles, 96 paginated blog pages, replicated across 75+ languages), free multi-platform entry tier, and 100k+ Android install base.

product.core_features: Upload lab report as PDF/JPG/PNG (up to 10MB) or manual value entry; AI analysis in ~60 seconds; 40-45 page PDF report; 15,000+ biomarker term lexicon across CBC, metabolic panels, liver, kidney, thyroid, lipids, iron, vitamins, hormones, inflammation, HbA1c, tumor markers; abnormal-value highlighting; trend tracking and multi-test comparison; 7-day AI nutrition meal plans; supplement recommendations with dosage/timing; family health history tool (14 relationship types x 8 health categories) with hereditary pattern analysis; family profile seats (2-5 depending on tier); 75+ interface languages (100+ via API); 'health risk assessment and disease prediction scores' (iOS description); API v11 + white-label enterprise offering
product.signature_differentiator: No other player combines: (1) machine-scale multilingual programmatic SEO — ~960 long-tail biomarker articles per language ('High AST symptoms', 'Borderline triglycerides') published daily across 75+ languages, all bylined 'Prof. Dr. Thomas Klein' (the CMO), engineered to capture every symptom/biomarker Google query including BR; (2) a charity free-access program (kantesti.org) with human-reviewed applications — genuine PR/positioning moat; (3) free Chrome extension + free web/iOS/Android entry points; (4) claimed 15,000-biomarker lexicon in 75+ languages. The moat is distribution and language coverage, not clinical depth.
product.lab_data_handling: Upload-only: patient photographs/exports a PDF or image, or types values. No lab integrations, no LIS connections, no EMR pull in the consumer product (HL7 v2.x/FHIR R4/CDA/Epic/Cerner appear only as RFP talking points in the B2B buyer's guide, with no evidence of live deployments). Claims 10,000+ lab report format templates recognized. No retest cadence guidance, no hardware, no at-home testing, no CGM/wearable ingestion — purely transactional per uploaded report.
product.family_dependents_depth: Family support exists but is shallow: premium tiers add profile seats (2 users on 6-report bundle, 5 on annual; homepage says 3 — inconsistent) and a family health history questionnaire (14 relationship types, 8 health categories) feeding 'hereditary pattern' analysis. No pediatric reference ranges, no real caregiver/proxy management workflow, no per-dependent view of trends, no hereditary-risk clinical escalation — seats are sharing accounts, not a dependents model. This remains an open flank for Dr. Exame's family pillar.
product.doctor_sharing: [uncertain] No dedicated doctor portal, consultation brief, or SOAP-style export found in any consumer-facing material; reports are positioned as 'discussion preparation' the patient brings to a licensed clinician (40-45 page PDF is the artifact). The doctor-facing motion is B2B instead: selling interpretation to labs/clinics/telehealth via API/white-label. Nothing resembling a doctor-facing view or share-link workflow was found.
product.action_loop_monetization: Post-interpretation loop = nutrition + supplements: 7-day AI meal plans and supplement recommendations with dosing/interaction notes are the paid-tier hooks (no affiliate partners disclosed — undisclosed supplement funnel is plausible). Second loop: enterprise API/white-label upsell pitched to labs, hospitals, insurers. No telemedicine, no prescriptions, no imaging/MCED marketplace. Monetization is per-report/annual-credits with relentless discount codes (VIP60), i.e., conversion happens at interpretation time, not after.

technology.ai_approach: Claims a 'proprietary neural network with 2.38 trillion parameters' — no architecture paper, no model card, almost certainly an LLM pipeline wrapper (unverified). No per-report human review. Clinical governance is claimed via CMO 'Thomas Klein, MD, clinical hematologist, full-time employee' plus a 4-name advisory board (Mitchell, Weber, Rodriguez, Chen — generic names, no verifiable institutional affiliations found; buyer's guide separately claims 50+ physicians). Validation is an internal automated benchmark (see trust section), self-published to GitHub and Figshare (DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.32095435), explicitly not peer-reviewed.
technology.data_inputs: Lab report files (PDF/JPG/PNG), manual biomarker entry, and the family health history questionnaire. Nothing else: no wearables, no CGM, no genomics, no continuous data, no patient-record integrations.
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: web app, iOS, Android, Chrome extension (file upload + manual entry) and API v11. Exhaustion: 40-45 page PDF report, account-synced cross-platform report storage. Enterprise marketing claims HL7 v2.x, FHIR R4, CDA/C-CDA, SMART on FHIR — no evidence of live integrations. Conspicuously absent for a 75-language product: Apple Health Records, Health Connect, RNDS/REL (Brazil), WhatsApp ingestion, any LIS connector, any FHIR endpoint documented in the public API docs. Broad language coverage but narrow interoperability surface.
technology.platform: Web (kantesti.net) + iOS App Store (125 countries, id6751127324, category Medical, v1.1.1, updated 2026-05-02) + Google Play (com.aibloodtestanalyzer.app, 100k+ downloads) + Chrome extension + B2B API (v11). Apple privacy label: collects identifiers, health data, contact info (name/email/address/phone), photos, diagnostics.

ux.onboarding: 'Analyze Now — Free' without credit card; free analysis of one report in ~60 seconds is the time-to-value hook; PDF export, trends, nutrition and family profiles sit behind the paywall. Marketing copy promises results 'without waiting days for a doctor appointment'.
ux.data_visualization: Abnormal values highlighted in a 40-45 page PDF report; trend tracking across multiple tests (basic on 6-bundle, 'advanced trend analysis and predictions' on annual); test-to-test comparison. iOS description mentions 'health risk assessment and disease prediction scores' but no public example of a dashboard/score UI was verifiable from listings — visualization depth appears report-centric rather than app-centric.
ux.engagement_channel: [uncertain] Appears transactional: account + cross-platform report sync is the retention mechanic; no community, streaks, reminders/nudges, push campaigns, or WhatsApp presence found. ~960-article blog + newsletter is the acquisition/SEO channel rather than in-product engagement. Classic lab-app pattern they criticize in their own B2B guide ('apps open on the result and churn') is arguably true of their own consumer product.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Weakest flank. (1) Accuracy numbers conflict across their own pages: 98.7% clinical accuracy (buyer's guide), 98,71% (multilingual press releases), 99.80% composite (validation page), 99.84% 'concordance with board-certified physicians across 20M+ de-identified cases' (best-of page). (2) Published methodology is an INTERNAL automated benchmark on 100,000 SYNTHETIC cases, composite score = 35% output-structure validity + 55% clinical-keyword recall + 10% latency — their own validation page states it is 'a technical evaluation, not a clinical trial or regulatory validation' and measures structured output, not diagnostic accuracy (kantesti.org admits the same). (3) 'Stanford AI Laboratory independent validation' appears only in Kantesti's own press releases; no Stanford source exists. (4) Advisory board and CMO identities unverifiable. (5) Scale claims (2M users, 50k doctors, 2.5M tests) are impossible for a company incorporated March 2026. (6) A 'multicenter trial, 10,000 patients, 42% error reduction' is cited with no trial registration or publication. (7) Trustpilot 4.0 from only 21 reviews; iOS 4.8 from 5 ratings — thin social proof. (8) Billing transparency: permanent 60% 'VIP' discount codes, crypto payments, and a refund guarantee that Trustpilot volume is too small to corroborate. Benchmark of credibility risks: synthetic-case self-benchmark marketed as '98.71% clinical accuracy' is the textbook example of an unsubstantiated clinical claim.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Self-positioned below device line: 'NOT currently CE or UKCA marked', 'not classified as a medical device', 'informational support only', does not diagnose/treat/screen/predict/monitor. Disclaimers are consistent and prominent across web and app stores. But the same surfaces market 'disease prediction scores' and 'risk predictions' (iOS description) and '98.71% clinical accuracy' — claims that edge toward SaMD territory under ANVISA RDC 657/2022 and EU MDR if enforced. No ANVISA registration or Brazil-specific compliance found; no LGPD-specific treatment, DPO, or BR data-residency language located (UK company, UK/EU framing only). For Dr. Exame: their not-CE/not-UKCA posture and synthetic-only validation confirms that a real methodology page + LGPD-native posture is a differentiator, while their prediction-claims expose them to regulatory attack surface Dr. Exame deliberately avoids.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What Kantesti does NOT do (Dr. Exame openings): no doctor portal/consultation brief/SOAP export; no pediatric reference ranges or true dependent/caregiver management (family = sharing seats); no WhatsApp channel (the BR retention surface); no PIX/BRL pricing (BR payment friction — USD checkout + crypto only); no RNDS/lab/LIS integrations; no human-in-the-loop review; no published, reviewable methodology; no continuous monitoring (upload-only transactions); no real community. What works (inspiration, not copy): programmatic long-tail SEO on biomarker/symptom queries in PT (~960 articles) — Dr. Exame could own BR-specific queries (SUS, Dasa/Fleury report formats, 'como ler exame X') with fewer, higher-trust articles; free tier as top-of-funnel; Chrome extension as zero-friction surface; kantesti.org charity program as reputation play; 125-country App Store coverage from day one; buyer's-guide 2026 as B2B door-opener. Counter-positioning: their trust profile (5-month-old shell, 24-year-old sole director in Turkey, synthetic benchmark sold as clinical accuracy, unverifiable advisory board) is fragile — a credibility war ('published methodology vs. their 98,71%') favors Dr. Exame.
trust_gaps.relevance: HIGH — most active direct threat to Dr. Exame's freemium: free web+iOS+Android+Chrome entry, PT-BR content farm ranking on biomarker interpretation queries plus the B2B 'Guia do Comprador 2026', and headline 98,71% accuracy claims without published methodology. Mitigating factors: zero BR payment/WhatsApp localization, shallow family/doctor features, and a demonstrably weak trust foundation that enables credibility-based counter-positioning.
